findings.checklist_item: Resolve the AC-3 fork by specifying that --reason on a plain (non-force) close is REFUSED with a message pointing to --force/--force-close (rather than leaving 'documented effect' as an option that recreates the inert-flag defect).
evidence: AC: 'Passing --reason on a plain (non-force) close either has a documented effect or is refused — it must not be silently accepted and dropped'
Plan title/goal: 'Make transition --reason honest'

Under --force, reason is genuinely used (transition.py:325 note = (force_reason or reason or ...)); on a plain close it flows only into the never-read close_reason param (txn.py:188), so a 'documented effect' branch has no live sink to attach to without re-introducing behaviour ed13 removed
findings.finding: AC-3 leaves the plain-close --reason behaviour as an unresolved design fork ('either has a documented effect or is refused'), and one branch of that fork ('documented effect', i.e. accept-and-document-as-inert) would partially recreate the very honesty defect the plan targets — a flag accepted but not recorded. The plan's own honesty rationale points to refusal as the correct, structurally-cleaner choice; leaving both open invites the weaker outcome.
scenarios: Implementer picks the 'documented effect' branch and documents --reason on a plain close as accepted-but-inert, leaving a semantically dishonest flag
Two implementers diverge on the fork, producing inconsistent CLI behaviour across follow-up work
